documents.title: Initial Emergency Department Consultation
documents.content_text: Patient presents with acute subretinal and epigastric discomfort radiating to left scapula. Past medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Blood pressure 148/92 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm. EKG demonstrates non-specific ST segment abnormalities.

diagnostic_reports.conclusion: Trace proteinuria detected, negative for leukocytes and nitrites.

documents.title: Inpatient Discharge Summary
documents.content_text: 31-year-old female admitted for acute exacerbation of severe asthma. Responded favorably to systemic intravenous corticosteroid pulse therapy and bronchodilator nebulization. Peak expiratory flow improved from 210 L/min to 420 L/min. Discharged on fluticasone/salmeterol inhaler with outpatient pulmonology follow-up.

diagnostic_reports.conclusion: Bilateral hyperinflation without focal consolidation, pneumothorax, or pleural effusion.

documents.title: Cardiology Progress Note
documents.content_text: Follow-up for known ischemic cardiomyopathy. Patient reports mild exertional dyspnea when climbing two flights of stairs. Orthopnea denied. Medication adherence to carvedilol and lisinopril confirmed. Plan: continue current guideline-directed medical therapy.

documents.title: Neurology Outpatient Evaluation
documents.content_text: Patient presents with persistent hemicranial throbbing headaches accompanied by photophobia and nausea for 3 weeks. Visual aura noted prior to episodes. Neurological exam reveals intact cranial nerves II-XII, symmetrical reflexes. Recommended MRI Brain with contrast.

diagnostic_reports.code_display: MRI Brain with and without IV contrast
diagnostic_reports.conclusion: No acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, or abnormal parenchymal enhancement. Mild scattered non-specific white matter microvascular changes.
